title: Orange Curd
subtitle: Sweet, fragrant curd with a milder set than lemon
excerpt: Orange curd is gentler than lemon, sweeter, more fragrant, less sharp. It needs added lemon juice to help the set. Vivid orange colour, and best eaten within 4 weeks. Makes two small jars.
sourceNotes: Pam Corbin, Preserves. Oranges have less citric acid than lemons; added lemon juice is needed to get a firm curd set.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 3 months. Defrost in the fridge overnight and stir before using.

glossaryTerms.definition: A heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of barely simmering water, used for delicate emulsions like curd that would scramble over direct heat.

content.text: Orange curd is the sweeter, more fragrant sibling of lemon curd,  same butter-and-egg base, but with the juice and zest of oranges. Because oranges are less acidic than lemons, lemon juice is added to give the eggs something to set against. The result is a smooth, vivid orange curd. Makes about two 200 g jars.
Put the orange juice, lemon juice, orange zest, sugar, and butter in a heatproof
a pan of barely simmering water. Stir until the butter melts and the sugar dissolves fully.
Add the eggs and cook until thick

Add the beaten eggs and stir constantly with a wooden spoon or silicone spatula. Keep the water at a low simmer,  it should not bubble hard. Cook for 15 to 20 minutes until the curd thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon and hold a clear line when you draw your finger across it.
Pour through a fine sieve into hot sterilised jars to remove the zest and any cooked strands. Seal immediately and leave to cool. Orange curd thickens considerably as it cools.

items.cause: Oranges have more natural sugar than lemons.
items.fix: Reduce sugar to 120 g and increase lemon juice to 40 ml for a sharper, more balanced curd.

items.cause: Not enough acid, orange juice alone won't thicken the eggs as effectively as lemon.
items.fix: Increase lemon juice to 50 ml or use one extra egg yolk.

items.symptom: Colour is pale, not bright orange
items.cause: Pale oranges, often winter crop, give less colour.
items.fix: For a deeper colour, use 2 tbsp of freshly squeezed blood orange juice in addition to the standard orange juice.

items.cause: Not enough citrus to balance the egg flavour.
items.fix: Add an extra tablespoon of orange juice. Curds made without lemon as the primary acid can taste eggy at lower acid levels.

content.text: Refrigerate immediately. Use within 4 weeks. Freezes for up to 3 months.
